title: Gateway strips API key org-scope, enabling intermittent cross-org access
creator: Marco Chen
description: Summary: Several Dedicated and Private customers reported intermittent cross-organization access after an API key rotation or a proxy failover. In affected requests, the downstream service observed an API call bound to the wrong org (customer A's API key accepted as customer B). This occurred across Hosted gateway shim, Dedicated ingress, and Private on-prem proxies. Impact: potential data crossing between customers, triggering urgent escalation by 2 enterprise customers. Immediate mitigation: temporary rolling revert of last gateway change in prod-edge and disabling apikey-to-session backfill in the Private router.
reproduction_steps: Create two orgs (OrgA, OrgB) with API keys apikey-A and apikey-B
Trigger a rotation for apikey-A while traffic is routed through the gateway shim that performs apikey->session conversion and attaches org headers
Simultaneously cause a proxy restart (simulated by draining the gateway instance) to create timing overlap between cache invalidation and rebind flows
Observe that some requests carrying apikey-A are accepted with OrgB context (service sees X-Redwood-Org: org-b or org claim in token)
root_cause_summary: Race between gateway's apikey metadata cache invalidation and the apikey->session backfill flow. When cache entries are evicted during rotation, a fallback metadata lookup path returned stale mapping from a shared metadata service in rare edge timing windows. Additionally, the gateway was stripping the authoritative org binding from the signed token when forwarding, relying only on a mutable header that could be overwritten by intermediate proxies.
short_term_mitigation: Reverted recent gateway change that relaxed org binding propagation (deployed 2026-03-02)
Disabled apikey->session automatic backfill in Private routers until fix (2026-03-03)
Added strict header validation in canary: reject requests where token introspection org != X-Redwood-Org header
long_term_fix_plan: Make org binding canonical in signed tokens (include org_id claim and signature check at every hop)
Stop relying on mutable headers for org scoping; introduce X-Redwood-Signed-Org header that contains signed metadata verified by service layer
Linearize apikey metadata updates: introduce a small version stamp and compare-and-swap update path for rotation to avoid stale reads
Improve cache consistency: change TTL and add explicit invalidation broadcast for Dedicated pools
Add end-to-end tests covering rotation+proxy-failover windows and integrate into CI
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy signature verification and cache linearization to staging. 2) Canary deploy to one region (us-west-2) with traffic slice 1%. 3) Monitor token-introspection mismatch metric and SLOs for 48h. 4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% over 72h if no regressions. 5) Re-enable apikey->session backfill after validation.
